The CEMAC QR Code standard, launched 29 July 2026 across six states including Cameroon, lets a client with a bank account, mobile money wallet or microfinance account pay by scan whatever their institution.
GIMACPAY, the CEMAC card-mobile-transfer ecosystem in service since 2021, processed over sixteen million mobile transactions in 2025.
BEAC says the QR code launched 29 July 2026 lets any bank or microfinance mobile app read any merchant's code regardless of institution or CEMAC country.
Le Jour reports the Camtel director saying Camtel will enter the competitive mobile money market in Cameroon with the Blue Money brand, launch date not yet known.
COBAC's 2025 annual report, as relayed by Ecomatin, counts 2.95 billion payment operations in 2025 through licensed payment institutions (Orange Money Cameroun and Mobile Money Corporation (MTN)).
GIMAC said that in the first half of 2026 payment institutions and mobile money operators, with Cameroonian operators among the main contributors, dominate GIMACPAY transaction volumes.
GIMACPAY links 56 banks, 26 microfinance institutions, 16 payment institutions and mobile money operators and 52 aggregators across the CEMAC, which processed 20.3 million transactions in 2025.

MTN Cameroun and Orange Cameroun mobile money operators processed 1.50 million and 1.12 million issued transactions in H1 2026, and Orange and MTN lead acquiring with 4.46 million and 3.14 million, per GIMAC.

MTN Cameroon's Mobile Money Corporation runs MoMo accounts on which it presented MoMo Helep Pro, offering employees digital advances up to 100,000 FCFA repayable in 30 days, and a Bulk Payment system for instant mass payments, per Le Jour.

Gimacpay links 95 participants including 53 banks, 11 mobile money operators, the Cameroonian Treasury and 16 aggregators, and processed 12 million transactions worth 601.7 billion FCFA by 31 December 2023 per BEAC data.
